angularDiameterSource: Uniform-disc fit to the 780 averaged squared visibilities of the pinned February 2020 VLT/MATISSE continuum data (3.94-4.00 um), this package; Drevon et al. (2024, MNRAS Letters 527, L88) report 43.8 mas for the same epoch and 42.5 mas for December 2018.
radiusSource: Joyce et al. (2020): 764 (+116/-62) solar radii at 695700 km. The pinned angular diameter at the adopted distance gives 767 solar radii, 0.4 percent larger.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Effective temperature 3600 ± 25 K from Levesque & Massey 2020 (ApJL 891, L37; https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.10463), abstract and Section 3: MARCS model fits to optical spectrophotometry of 15 February 2020, during the Great Dimming. The radius source, Joyce et al. 2020, adopts this value in its Table 2.

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius. The photosphere of a red supergiant is not a solid surface and its limb is not sharp; the sphere is the reference surface the interferometric image is cast onto, not a measured shape.

surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/betelgeuse.json: -0.079
companionSource: Montargès et al. (2026, A&A 711, L12; https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202661023): the candidate companion detected at 6.1 sigma on 6 December 2024 in the SPHERE-ZIMPOL CntHa filter, 52.32 +/- 0.18 mas from Betelgeuse at position angle 117.12 +/- 0.60 degrees, at (8.24 +/- 1.04) x 10^-4 of the star’s brightness in that filter. Howell et al. (2025, ApJ 988, L47; https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.15749) saw it three days later at 52 +/- 2 mas and 115 +/- 5 degrees, at 1.5 sigma, and proposed the name; the IAU Working Group on Star Names adopted Siwarha for Alpha Orionis B on 22 September 2025 (https://exopla.net/star-names/modern-iau-star-names/). The paper calls it a candidate: that it is bound to Betelgeuse awaits a second epoch.
companionOrbitalPeriodSource: MacLeod et al. (2025, ApJ 978, 50; https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.11332), Table 1: 2109.2 (+9.2/-9.1) d, from radial velocities measured between 1896 and 2024.
